title: Ivo and the Vector
premise: Orsen Vasquez tends a half-built terraforming garden and an ancient beacon on a forgotten colony world, until the beacon receives a manifest from a ship that was destroyed decades ago — carrying a passenger name that shouldn't exist. The name belongs to Ivo, a courier who smuggled out the proof that the war's opening atrocity was staged by Orsen's own government, and whose message is still locked in the beacon's core. As a military task force descends to erase the evidence and the reactor beneath the garden begins an unexplained countdown, Orsen must choose between the loyalty they owe the colony that raised them and the truth that could end the war. Orsen broadcasts Ivo's message at the last moment, forcing both sides to a ceasefire, but the countdown's true purpose — a dead-man's archive Ivo left as insurance — means the price of survival is Orsen's name, home, and history, traded for a peace they may never be credited with.
about_author: B. M. Brightwater is the pen name of a former hydrologist who spent six years on remote environmental monitoring stations before turning to fiction. They write quiet, character-driven science fiction about people who maintain the machinery of hope.

chapters.title: The Garden for No One
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Establishes daily life tending the terraforming greenhouse and the beacon tower on half-terraformed Kepler's Rest. Orsen talks to seedlings meant for grandchildren not yet born. Emotional beat: lonely devotion, a life built on deferred purpose.

chapters.title: Manifest of the Meridian
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The beacon, silent for forty years, prints a cargo manifest from the Meridian, a ship that burned on launch. One passenger name is unfamiliar: Ivo Ren. Orsen reports it and is told to forget it. Emotional beat: unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: The Name That Shouldn't Be
chapters.summary: Orsen investigates colony records; the name Ivo Ren matches a sealed file older than the colony charter. An old archivist, Sefa, hints the Meridian never crashed — it was scuttled. Emotional beat: first crack in Orsen's trust in authority.

chapters.title: Visitors in Uniform
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. A military survey team arrives, polite and wrong, asking about beacon transmissions. Sefa covers for Orsen and recognizes the commander's insignia from the war's darkest unit. Emotional beat: dread of the past arriving wearing a smile.

chapters.title: Signal in the Core
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen finds a physical data core bolted inside the beacon — not colony hardware. It's warm. It's waiting for a handshake code. Emotional beat: the thrill and terror of holding something someone died to hide.

chapters.title: What Sefa Buried
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Flashback chapter: Sefa helped load the Meridian's true cargo — Ivo Ren, a war-crimes courier — and has spent forty years pretending otherwise. Emotional beat: guilt calcified into duty.

chapters.title: The Handshake
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen cracks the handshake using the manifest's coordinates and gets a fragment: Ivo's message, half-decrypted, accusing the government of staging the atrocity that started the war. Emotional beat: vertigo — the war's cause was a lie.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The reactor beneath the garden self-initializes a countdown — triggered by the core's activation. Seventy-two hours. The task force's shuttle burns down through the atmosphere. Emotional beat: consequences arriving all at once.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Gardener
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Commander Adeyemi questions Orsen gently, offering protection in exchange for the core. Orsen lies for the first time in their life — and realizes Adeyemi knows they're lying. Emotional beat: loyalty and truth pulling apart.

chapters.title: Sefa's Confession
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa tells Orsen the whole truth about Ivo Ren and the scuttled Meridian, and asks Orsen to destroy the core instead of sending it. Emotional beat: love expressed as a request to stay safe and small.

chapters.title: The Colony Votes
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Orsen brings the choice to the colony council: send the message and invite retaliation, or bury it and keep the fragile peace. The vote splits. Emotional beat: a community discovering it was built on someone else's silence.

chapters.title: Sabotage in the Greenhouse
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Someone destroys a third of the garden and steals the core's backup key — one of their own, working for Adeyemi. Orsen suspects their closest friend, Dara. Emotional beat: betrayal inside the family they chose.

chapters.title: Dara's Price
chapters.summary: Dara's POV. Dara's brother is a POW; Adeyemi promised his release for the key. Dara justifies the theft, then sees the staged-atrocity evidence and breaks. Emotional beat: survival's cost measured in other people.

chapters.title: Seventeen Hours
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. With the key gone, Orsen must decrypt the message manually from fragments while Adeyemi's team seizes the beacon tower. Reactor countdown accelerates. Emotional beat: racing the clock with bleeding hands.

chapters.title: The Truth About the Reactor
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa realizes the countdown isn't a weapon — it's Ivo's dead-man archive, set to broadcast the full message to both war fleets unless physically suppressed. Adeyemi isn't here to stop a bomb; she's here to stop the truth. Emotional beat: the trap inverts.

chapters.title: Storming the Beacon
chapters.summary: Orsen and Dara, reconciled but raw, infiltrate the occupied tower through the garden's root tunnels. Sefa creates a diversion and is captured. Emotional beat: loyalty redefined — not obedience, but standing together.

chapters.title: Adeyemi's War
chapters.summary: Adeyemi's POV. Her own chapter: she lost everyone in the staged atrocity and has spent the war hunting the proof she half-wants to be false. She offers Orsen a deal one last time. Emotional beat: the enemy revealed as a mirror.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Climax. With the countdown at zero and Adeyemi's soldiers breaching the core room, Orsen completes the handshake. Ivo's message — voice, evidence, and a plea — transmits to every fleet in the system. Emotional beat: a held breath becoming a shout.

chapters.title: Silence After the Signal
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Fleets hold fire. Adeyemi stands down, arrests her own handlers instead. The colony waits to learn if truth was worth it. Emotional beat: exhausted, suspended hope.

chapters.title: The Price Named
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The ceasefire holds, but the government disavows the colony; supply lines close. The garden will die. Orsen accepts exile as the messenger no one wants to look at. Emotional beat: grief with a straight spine.

chapters.title: What the Garden Grows Next
chapters.summary: Orsen and Dara's POV. The colonists vote to leave Kepler's Rest together, taking seeds and the beacon's archive with them. Sefa, released, chooses to stay as caretaker of the record. Emotional beat: survival as a shared act.

chapters.title: Ivo and the Vector
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, epilogue. Aboard the colony ship, Orsen receives a final beacon ping: a reply from Ivo Ren — alive, old, somewhere far — one line: 'Thank you for watering it.' Orsen plants the first seed in the ship's bay. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope.
